text: if I go into it and I have no idea how we'll acquire those customers, I'm not real confident I'll figure it out when I'm there.
speaker: Sean Ellis
context: Lenny asks Sean about his approach to helping companies figure out growth strategy. Sean explains that even though he focuses on activation and onboarding first, he still develops early hypotheses about customer acquisition channels before taking on a project. He wants to have 2-3 viable acquisition ideas going in, knowing he'll likely discover more, so that at least one channel will work profitably.
text_ko: 제가 그 일에 뛰어들어서 어떻게 고객을 획득(customer acquisition)할지 전혀 감이 안 오면, 가서 그때 가서 알아내겠다는 자신감이 별로 없어요.
text_zh: 要是我一进去就完全不知道怎么把那些客户拉到手，我就不太有把握到时候能想得出办法。
text_es: Si me lanzo y no tengo ni idea de cómo vamos a captar a esos clientes, dudo que lo vaya a resolver sobre la marcha.
key_sentence: if I go into it and I have no idea how we'll acquire those customers, I'm not real confident I'll figure it out when I'm there.
original_text: When I go in and directly am involved with a company on the acquisition side, I am thinking about my hypotheses on the acquisition pretty early on, because if I go into it and I have no idea how we'll acquire those customers, I'm not real confident I'll figure it out when I'm there.

vocabulary.definition: To obtain or gain possession of something, often through effort or purchase.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'acquire' frequently refers to gaining new customers, assets, or companies, often as part of a growth strategy or merger.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'acquire' can imply a straightforward transaction, it may also suggest a strategic effort to enhance market position or capabilities.

text: Customer acquisition is so hard that if you're not really efficient at converting and retaining and monetizing people, you're going to really struggle on the customer acquisition side.
speaker: Sean Ellis
context: Sean explains his prioritization approach to growth - focusing first on activation, then engagement and referrals, then revenue optimization, and only lastly on customer acquisition. He argues that in today's competitive environment, companies must be extremely efficient at converting, retaining, and monetizing customers before they can succeed at scalable customer acquisition.
text_ko: 고객 획득(customer acquisition)이 워낙 힘들어서, 전환(converting)·유지(retaining)·수익화(monetizing)을 효율적으로 못하면 고객 확보 쪽에서 진짜 고생해요.
text_zh: 获客这么难，如果你在转化、留存和变现这块做得不够好的话，那获客这边你肯定会很吃力。
text_es: Conseguir clientes nuevos es tan difícil que si no eres realmente eficiente convirtiendo, reteniendo y monetizando a la gente, te va a costar muchísimo en el lado de adquisición de clientes.
key_sentence: You're going to really struggle on customer acquisition without efficient monetizing people.

vocabulary.definition: The process of attracting and converting new customers to purchase a company's products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, customer acquisition is critical for growth, often involving strategies like marketing campaigns, sales tactics, and customer relationship management.
vocabulary.nuance: While it emphasizes the initial engagement, it is often discussed in conjunction with retention strategies to ensure long-term success.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving maximum productivity with minimum wasted effort or expense.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, being efficient means optimizing processes to reduce costs and increase output, which is essential for competitiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a positive connotation, suggesting not just speed but also effectiveness in resource use.

vocabulary.definition: The process of converting an asset, service, or product into a source of revenue.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, monetizing often refers to strategies for generating income from users, such as through subscriptions, advertising, or sales.
vocabulary.nuance: It implies a strategic approach to generating profit, and is often discussed in the context of balancing user experience with revenue generation.

text: If you start paying attention to what your somewhat disappointed users are telling you and then you start tweaking onboarding and product based on their feedback, maybe you're going to dilute it for your must have users.
speaker: Sean Ellis
context: Lenny asks what to do when only 10% of users would be very disappointed without the product. Sean advises ignoring users who say they'd be 'somewhat disappointed' because they view the product as nice-to-have. He warns that optimizing for these users might make the product good for everyone but great for no one, potentially weakening its value for the core must-have users.
text_ko: 다소 실망한 사용자들이 하는 말에 귀 기울여 그 피드백을 바탕으로 온보딩(onboarding)과 제품을 조금씩 손봐서 맞추기 시작하면, 오히려 핵심 사용자들(must-have users)에게는 제품의 강점이 희석될 수 있어요.
text_zh: 如果你开始关注那些有点失望的用户的反馈，然后根据他们的意见去调整用户引导(onboarding)和产品，可能会让你的核心用户体验变差。
text_es: Si empiezas a hacerle caso a lo que te dicen los usuarios que están medio decepcionados y luego te pones a ajustar el onboarding y el producto basándote en sus comentarios, a lo mejor vas a terminar diluyendo la experiencia para tus usuarios que realmente no pueden vivir sin tu producto.
key_sentence: Paying attention to disappointed users may dilute it for must-have users.

vocabulary.definition: Making small adjustments or modifications to improve something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, tweaking often refers to refining processes, products, or strategies based on user feedback or performance metrics.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests minor changes rather than major overhauls, implying a careful and thoughtful approach to improvement.

vocabulary.definition: Information or criticism about a product, service, or performance, used as a basis for improvement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup environment, feedback is crucial for product development and customer satisfaction, guiding decisions on enhancements and features.
vocabulary.nuance: Feedback can be positive or negative, and it is often seen as a valuable tool for growth when solicited and acted upon appropriately.

vocabulary.definition: To weaken or lessen the strength or effectiveness of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, diluting a product or service can refer to making changes that may reduce its appeal or core value to a specific audience.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting that the essence or quality of something is being compromised.

text: Half the people feel like we're years from having this product ready to grow, and half the people are like, 'What are we waiting for?
speaker: Sean Ellis
context: Lenny asks about how firm the 40% threshold is in the Sean Ellis test. Sean explains that having a specific target like 40% helps align teams on when to start scaling growth efforts. Without this alignment, startup teams often split between those who think the product needs years more work and those eager to start growing immediately.
text_ko: 우리 팀의 절반은 이 제품이 제대로 성장할 준비가 되려면 아직 몇 년은 더 걸릴 것 같다고 느끼고, 나머지 절반은 “뭘 더 기다리고 있는 거예요?”라고 해요.
text_zh: 一半人觉得我们离把这个产品做好、开始放量还有好几年，另一半人却在说：我们还等什么？
text_es: La mitad cree que estamos a años de tener este producto listo para escalar (grow), y la otra mitad dice: "¿a qué esperamos?"
key_sentence: Half the people feel like we're years from having this product ready to grow.
original_text: I think one of the biggest challenges in an early stage startup is half the people feel like we're years from having this product ready to grow, and half the people are like, 'What are we waiting for?' Where if you can actually get people on the same page of what does product market fit look like for our business, and it's at that point that we're going to.

text: Even when I first moved to Silicon Valley, I remember the conversations back at LogMeIn in the mid 2000s of kind of like, 'When do we step on the gas?
speaker: Sean Ellis
context: Sean continues explaining why having a clear product-market fit threshold is important for startup teams. He shares how even before the term 'product-market fit' existed, his team at LogMeIn in the mid-2000s struggled with the same fundamental question of when exactly to start aggressively scaling their growth efforts.
text_ko: 실리콘밸리로 처음 이사했을 때도 기억해요. 2000년대 중반 LogMeIn 다닐 때 '언제 본격적으로 속도를 내야 할까요?' 같은 얘기들이 오갔어요.
text_zh: 刚搬到硅谷的时候，我还记得2000年代中期在 LogMeIn 那边的讨论，基本上都是在问：“我们什么时候该加速（step on the gas）？”
text_es: Recuerdo que cuando me mudé a Silicon Valley por primera vez, en LogMeIn a mediados de los años 2000, las conversaciones eran más o menos así: «¿Cuándo pisamos el acelerador?»
key_sentence: When do we step on the gas?
original_text: Even when I first moved to Silicon Valley, I remember the conversations back at LogMeIn in the mid 2000s of kind of like, 'When do we step on the gas? What is the combination of factors that need to be in place before we start pouring fuel on the early fire?'

vocabulary.definition: To accelerate or increase the pace of an activity or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in startups, this phrase often refers to intensifying efforts in marketing, product development, or scaling operations to achieve growth.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase conveys a sense of urgency and proactive action, and is typically used in contexts where speed is critical to success.

text: I think basically for each business it's just thinking about what's unique for that business that is going to open up channel opportunities and everyone's going to be a little bit, I think jaded from whatever the last thing that worked really well.
speaker: Sean Ellis
context: Lenny asks how to help businesses figure out which growth channel to focus on - whether paid acquisition, SEO, sales, or virality. Sean explains that each business has unique characteristics that make certain channels more viable, and warns that people often get biased by their previous successful experiences and try to apply the same approach to different businesses.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 기본적으로 각 비즈니스는 자기만의 고유한 게 뭔지 생각해서 그걸로 채널 기회(channel opportunities)를 만들어내는 게 중요해요. 그리고 사람들은 이전에 효과가 좋았던 것 때문에 다들 좀 식상해져 있을 거예요.
text_zh: 我觉得基本上每个生意都要想想，自己有什么独特的地方能开拓新的渠道机会，而且大家对之前那些很成功的做法多少都会有点审美疲劳。
text_es: Mira, creo que básicamente para cada negocio se trata de pensar qué es lo único de ese negocio que va a abrir oportunidades de canal, y todo el mundo va a estar un poco escamado por lo último que funcionó realmente bien.
key_sentence: Thinking about what's unique will open up channel opportunities despite being jaded from whatever worked well.

vocabulary.definition: Potential avenues or methods through which a business can reach its target market or distribute its products and services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying channel opportunities is crucial for optimizing marketing strategies and enhancing customer engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a proactive approach to exploring new markets or distribution methods, rather than relying solely on established channels.
